**The proposed policy works as intended on these challenge cases.** Accept
ordinary ML only when it passes convergence and PSD admissibility; otherwise
run PSD from its own FABIN3-auto start, without reusing ordinary estimates.
It matches direct PSD's success/failure outcomes and fitted objectives on all
120 saved datasets. Compared with the existing warm-start route, it gains two
targets and loses one.

## The important data

**Known targets reached, out of 20 datasets per row.** Both stages use
normalization. “Independent” means PSD constructs its own start.

```{r}
x <- read.csv('results/two-stage-cold/by_family.csv')
k <- expand.grid(design=c('ernst','weak_marker','high_r2'),batch=c('development','fresh'),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
x <- x[match(paste(k$batch,k$design),paste(x$batch,x$design)),]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Batch=ifelse(x$batch=='development','Earlier','Later'),
  Problem=unname(c(ernst='Ernst',weak_marker='Weak markers',high_r2='High R²')[x$design]),
  `Warm-start two-stage`=x$warm_hit, `Independent two-stage`=x$cold_hit,
  `Direct PSD`=x$direct_hit,check.names=FALSE),row.names=FALSE)
```

- **34 cases stop after ordinary ML; 86 need PSD.** All independently started
  PSD fits reproduce the saved direct-PSD results. Where ordinary ML is
  accepted, its objective also matches direct PSD; the largest discrepancy
  across returned pairs is below 1e-12.
- **Compared with warm starts:** two Ernst cases are recovered; one earlier
  weak-marker case is lost. There is no hidden retry or multistart.
- **Timing is now checked.** On this set, independent two-stage takes about
  27% more total time than direct PSD, but about 16% less than warm-start
  two-stage. The ordinary shortcut saves time on 34 cases; the other 86
  outweigh that saving. See the [timing summary](timing-summary.html).

**Verdict:** this is a reasonable, simpler interpretation of ordinary-first
PSD. These results provide no reason to require warm starts. They support
keeping independent fallback as a candidate policy; they do not establish
universal superiority. The library's existing warm-start implementation has
not been changed by this test.

Both stages use FABIN3-auto starts, matching the earlier comparison so that
only the handoff changes. Ordinary ML uses L-BFGS with information scaling;
PSD uses SLSQP with diagonal preconditioning. Each has 5,000 evaluations,
relative objective tolerance 1e-12 and parameter tolerance 1e-10. Target recovery
requires convergence, PSD accuracy/admissibility and the requested-chart check.
The 120 datasets are already-inspected development cases, not held-out evidence.
